name: How can I keep an older-home renovation from going over budget?

mainEntity.name: How can I keep an older-home renovation from going over budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: Set a realistic budget by separating essential repairs, functional improvements, and finish upgrades, then reserving room for conditions that cannot be confirmed before demolition. Context: older-home work may involve kitchens, bathrooms, additions, ADUs, garage conversions, or multiple systems at once. Key factors: scope, access, utility relocation, structural work, finish level, permit review, and whether the home remains occupied. Practical guidance: ask for allowances and exclusions in writing and identify decisions that can trigger a change in cost. Consider phasing, but confirm whether separate phases duplicate design, mobilization, or permit work. A clear priority list supports better decisions when discoveries occur.
acceptedAnswer.description: Divide the project into essential repairs, functional improvements, and optional finishes. Compare detailed scopes, define allowances and exclusions, reserve a contingency for concealed conditions, and decide in advance which upgrades can be postponed if discoveries increase the cost.
